newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lai Sun plans US$100 mln bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Lai Sun plans US$100 mln bond issue.

text.p: Lai Sun Development Co Ltd said on Tuesday its wholly owned subsidiary Lai Sun International Finance (Cayman Islands) Ltd planned to issue about US$100 million in bonds convertible into shares of Asia Television Ltd.
Lai Sun Development said in a statement the bonds would be issued for a term of seven years in the international capital markets to institutional and professional investors.
Pricing, timing and other terms of the issue have yet to be fixed and the exchange into Asia Television (ATV) stock would be subject to an initial public offering (IPO) of ATV shares.

"If the proposal proceeds, it is intended that the net proceeds of the issue of the bonds will be used by LSD (Lai Sun Development) and its subsidiaries for replenishing the LSD Group's land bank in Hong Kong and for general working capital purposes," Lai Sun Development said.
It said the proceeds would not be used to fund any financing requirements of ATV and its subsidiaries. Lai Sun Development has held a 16.67 percent stake in ATV since 1988.

ATV's main businesses are the broadcasting, production and sale, licensing and distribution of television programmes. It had net profit of HK$12.1 million in 1996 compared with a loss of HK$86.6 million in 1995. Turnover in 1996 was HK$999.1 million compared with HK$856.4 million.
Lai Sun Development said in the event of an IPO of ATV shares, bond holders would be able to exchange the bonds for the ATV shares held by the Lai Sun Development group.

"In the event that the bonds are exchanged, LSD will realise its interest in ATV. The directors of LSD consider that this is consistent with the LSD Group's intention to seek to unlock the intrinsic value of certain of its non-core assets through restructurings and spin-offs," it said.

If the value of the ATV shares held by the LSD Group is less than the principal amount of the bonds at the date dealing begins in ATV shares, Lai Sun Development said it would pay the difference in cash to bond holders.
Lai Sun Development chairman Lim Por Yen and deputy chairman Peter Lam Kin Ngok own about 50.83 percent of ATV shares.

Lai Sun Development said the directors, chief executive and substantial shareholders of the company and its controlling shareholder Lai Sun Garment (International) Ltd would not take up any bonds during the issue. The issue requires shareholder approval.
It said the coupon interest rate of the bonds is expected to be lower than the interest rate paid on its bank borrowings.
An application has been made to list the bonds on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange but no application would be made to list them on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, Lai Sun said.
